transit.description: Internal no-op graph edge (transit-node pattern). Retained for `types`: a Worker bound to another Worker over RPC generates types that embed the callee's source types (Service<import('../other/src/index').Foo>), so upstream source changes must invalidate `wrangler types` even though it reads only wrangler.jsonc.

check-types.description: Type-check with tsc -b. Uses ^check-types (NOT the transit node): every package sets composite:true, so `tsc -b` also builds its referenced projects. Running these in parallel makes several packages emit the same declarations and .tsbuildinfo concurrently, which races. Ordering along the dependency graph is required for correctness. Declaration emit is a byproduct of composite (all `exports` resolve to source .ts), so nothing is cached. No `types` edge: worker-configuration.d.ts is committed, so it is a tracked $TURBO_DEFAULT$ input and hashes directly - regenerating it here would dirty the tree mid-CI.

types.description: Regenerate the committed worker-configuration.d.ts (wrangler types). Writes a tracked source file, so it is uncached like the other write-mode tasks - run it after editing wrangler.jsonc, then commit the result. CI verifies freshness with types:check instead of running this.

types:check.description: Verify the committed worker-configuration.d.ts still matches wrangler.jsonc (wrangler types --check). Read-only and cached; fails when the file has drifted, prompting `make types` + commit. Unlike `types`, --check does not start workerd, so it is cheap in CI.

build.description: Build production output to dist/; gated on the package's own check-types and upstream builds.

dev.description: Run the local dev server (persistent, uncached).

preview.description: Serve the production build locally (persistent, uncached).

deploy.description: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers via wrangler (uncached). `check-types` gates workers that have no build step of their own (wrangler bundles from source); apps that upload build output add their own `build` edge in their package turbo.json.
